clues: This city in the east of the Kurdistan area of Iraq is ringed by hills and peaks. High ground stands to its north-east, south, and west.
Of the big towns in this land, this one has cooler summers and more wet winters. Snow can pile deep here, and it falls each year or two.
A Kurdish prince set up this city in the year 1784. His name was Ibrahim Pasha Baban.
For more than sixty years, this city led a Kurdish princedom. It was the chief seat of the Baban house till 1850.
The Azmar, Goizha, and Qaiwan peaks ring the city's north-east side. Baranan peak stands to the south, and low hills lie to the west.
